newsDocuments.headline: Pakistan’s largest oil refinery seeks up to $300 million in foreign financing for refinery upgrade: report

segments.text: Cnergyico Pakistan Limited, the country’s largest refiner, is seeking $150 million to $300 million in foreign project financing for its planned $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion refinery upgrade, with the company holding discussions with financi

“Phase 1 involves upgrading Motor Spirit (MS) and High Speed Diesel (HSD) production to Euro-V specifications, Phase 2 will focus on fuel oil conversion, and Phase 3 will cover capacity enhancement and port facilities,” read the note.
Management said the company was ahead of other domestic refineries in making progress on its upgrade plans, according to the research note.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil rises on Hormuz ship attacks, surplus supply outlook curbs gains

segments.text: HOUSTON: Oil prices edged higher on Tuesday in a choppy session as new attacks were reported on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, but gains were capped by an outlook for surplus global supplies.

Brent crude futures bounced off a session trough that was their lowest since August 27 and were up 45 cents, or 0.5 percent, to USD89.82 a barrel at 11:25 a.m. EDT (1625 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up 42 cents, or 0.
Brent’s session low was USD88.10 a barrel, while WTI slipped as low as USD79.07, pressured by a stock market slide.

newsDocuments.headline: India bonds inch higher as oil steadies ahead of RBI verdict

segments.text: MUMBAI: Indian government bonds edged up early on Wednesday, helped by softer oil prices and steady US Treasury yields, while traders avoided large bets before the Reserve Bank of India’s policy decision next week.

Softer oil prices, steady US Treasuries and a break in the benchmark 10-year yield below the 50-day moving average supported sentiment, though traders said demand remained subdued ahead of the RBI decision and key US economic data.
Brent crude was last at $90.16 per barrel, down $1 or 1.4% in Asian trade.

newsDocuments.headline: Palm oil falls on weaker soyoil, crude; Dalian gains limit losses

segments.text: JAKARTA: Malaysian palm oil futures declined on Wednesday, weighed down by weakness in Chicago soyoil and crude oil prices, while stronger Dalian rivals capped losses.
The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange lost 1 ringgit, or 0.02% to 4,239 ringgit a metric ton by the midday break.

Chicago Board of Trade soyoil futures kept up their downward momentum, which has restricted the bullish recovery in palm oil to some extent, said Anilkumar Bagani, commodity research head at Mumbai-based brokerage Sunvin Group.

newsDocuments.headline: Indian shares may open higher as foreign inflows, lower oil prices aid sentiment

segments.text: Indian shares are expected to open higher on Wednesday , recovering some of Monday’s losses, as foreign investors remained buyers in India and ​crude oil prices eased further, despite some renewed concerns over US ‌tariffs.
Meanwhile, Brent crude futures fell 0.7% to $90.8 per barrel on ​rising supply and the prospect of a market surplus. ​The ⁠prices are down about 23% so far in November.
